verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's first-party docs say escalation policies route incidents to users or schedules and notify one target at a time until someone acknowledges. Incidents are documented to escalate according to the service's escalation policy. A community comment corroborates fallback escalation tiers, but the evidence never documents the configurable delays or repeat rounds the story names. Missing for 10: documented escalation timeouts/delays between steps, documented repeat-round behavior, explicit multi-step level configuration detail.

support.subject: As an SRE, escalation policies walk unacknowledged pages through multiple steps — delays, fallback responders, and repeat rounds — until someone acknowledges

citations.quote: They are designed to notify a single target at a time until one individual acknowledges the incident.
The incident escalates in accordance with the service's escalation policy.
a service's escalation policy prompts notifications to on-call responders
Typically there was a fall-back escalation, and then it would go straight up the management chain
